items.title: Implications of EASO's New Obesity Definition Across Aging Cohorts: Prevalence and Associations With Dementia and All-Cause Mortality.
items.abstract: Although visceral adiposity and metabolic comorbidities may increase risks of dementia and mortality, the implications of the newly proposed European Association for the Study of Obesity (EASO) framework remain unclear. We aimed to describe the prevalence of obesity under the EASO framework vs traditional body mass index (BMI) criteria and to examine their associations with incident dementia and all-cause mortality. We used data from the English Longitudinal Study on Ageing (ELSA) and China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). Participants were classified using the EASO framework, which integrates BMI, waist-to-height ratio, and obesity-related comorbidities. Dementia was defined using validated algorithmic criteria or self-reported physician diagnosis; all-cause mortality was ascertained from death registries, medical records, or interviews with relatives. Associations between obesity phenotypes and outcomes were examined using Cox proportional hazards models, with cohort-specific hazard ratios (HRs) pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. Among 18,944 participants (mean age: ELSA 65.9 ± 9.3 years, CHARLS 58.2 ± 9.7 years; 54.3% and 53.2% female, respectively), 17,617 were included in the dementia analysis and 18,197 for mortality analysis, with a median follow-up of 8.2 years (CHARLS) and 11.5 years (ELSA). Under the EASO framework, 24.9% of CHARLS participants and 37.7% of ELSA participants were classified as obese. Compared with normal weight, EASO-defined overweight was associated with lower dementia (HR The EASO definition substantially reclassified obesity status in both Chinese and British older adults and revealed associations with dementia and mortality distinct from BMI alone. Although the observational design and self-reported dementia outcomes limited generalizability, our findings suggest that incorporating fat distribution and comorbidities assessment is crucial for clinical risk stratification.
items.summary_ja:
背景：内臓脂肪や代謝合併症は認知症や死亡リスクを高めるが、欧州肥満学会（EASO）が提唱した新たな肥満定義の影響は不明である。  
方法：イギリスの高齢者縦断研究（ELSA）と中国の健康退職縦断研究（CHARLS）データを用い、BMIに加え、ウエスト高比率や肥満関連合併症を統合したEASO基準で肥満を分類。認知症はアルゴリズムや医師診断の自己申告で判定し、全死亡は死亡登録や医療記録、家族面談で確認。肥満表現型と認知症・死亡リスクの関連をコックス比例ハザードモデルで解析し、メタ解析で統合。  
結果：18,944名（ELSA平均年齢65.9歳、CHARLS58.2歳）を対象に中央値8.2～11.5年追跡。EASO基準での肥満率はCHARLSで24.9%、ELSAで37.7%とBMI基準より高かった。EASO定義による過体重は認知症リスク低下と関連し、BMI単独とは異なる認知症・死亡との関連性を示した。  
結論：EASO基準は中国・英国の高齢者で肥満分類を大きく変え、脂肪分布や合併症を考慮することが臨床的リスク評価に重要であることを示唆する。ただし観察研究かつ自己申告の認知症評価には限界がある。
items.summary_short_ja: 本研究は、欧州肥満学会（EASO）の新たな肥満定義を用い、中国と英国の高齢者を対象に肥満の有病率と認知症・全死亡リスクとの関連を検討した。EASO基準はBMIに加え腹囲比や併存疾患を考慮し、従来のBMI基準より肥満者を多く分類。結果、EASO定義による過体重は認知症リスク低下と関連し、肥満の臨床的評価には脂肪分布と併存疾患の考慮が重要であることを示唆した。
